text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Denmark's two largest banks Den Danske Bank and Unidanmark could lose customers if third biggest BG Bank, mortgage credit firm Nykredit and insurer Topdanmark which already co-operate in a strategic alliance, merge to form one of Scandinavia's largest financial groups.

--- It is unlikely that Denmark or the other Nordic nations will send peacekeeping troops to participate in any multinational force for Zaire, Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen said at a Nordic Council meeting yesterday. He said Denmark preferred to contribute with humanitarian aid.

--- Denmark's windmill industry faces slower growth this year than in previous years due to a world market decline for windpower. The industry now estimates that total 1996 Danish turnover will be more than four billion crowns, up about ten percent on the previous year.
--- Maersk Air, a unit of Danish shipping, oil and gas group A.P. Moeller, is to challenge SAS by starting flights to six European cities from Aalborg in northern Denmark in January.

--- Denmark's largest shipbuilder, Lindoe Yard, risks demands from the European Commission to pay back about 250 million crowns in state subsidies, received in connection with the building of three ships. The vessels were sold to a Saudi Arabian shipping company in violation of EU subsidy rules.
